emerging_technology: LLM-based agentic AI that plans multi-step work, calls tools/APIs, observes results, and iterates with bounded human oversight.
intended_application: Customer-service intake and proposed account-change workflow, including address-change assistance and dispute intake, with human authorization for consequential account changes.
business_need: Reduce service handling time while maintaining identity, authorization, privacy, audit and compliance controls.
users_stakeholders: Customers, service agents, operations, compliance, fraud, information security, internal audit.
adoption_posture: Conservative / risk-averse for autonomous account-changing actions.
capabilities_constraints: Regulated systems; identity and authorization controls; audit requirements; strict data handling; change management and vendor-risk review.
risk_consequence_context: Incorrect or unauthorized actions can create customer harm, fraud, legal/compliance exposure and remediation costs.
management_question: Which agentic-AI landscape signals, incumbent controls and regulatory/identity dependencies matter most for bank service workflows, and what should management monitor before expanding agent authority?
time_horizon: 12-24 months; refresh at least quarterly and on material regulatory/standards changes.
additional_context: Contrast: same ET but regulated/high-consequence application. Relevant alternatives and monitoring triggers should shift toward deterministic workflows, supervised assistants, identity/authorization, audit and regulatory signals.
